title: Atomic Account Transfer Lock Scoping
prompt: Consider transferring money from Account A to Account B. A developer locks Account A, deducts ₹500, unlocks A, then locks Account B and adds ₹500. What race condition or consistency violation can an observer reading both balances encounter?

forbidden_misconceptions: individual locks are always sufficient for multi-resource transfer
deadlock is the only problem with multi-resource locks
evaluator_rubric.scoring_criteria: Learner must identify that an observer reading the sum of balances after the debit on A but before the credit on B will see that ₹500 has vanished from the system (violating atomicity and consistency). The transfer operation must be atomic across both accounts.
evaluator_rubric.ideal_response_summary: Between unlocking Account A and locking Account B, the system enters an inconsistent intermediate state. An auditing thread calculating total deposits across accounts during this window will observe ₹500 missing from the aggregate total balance. Both accounts must be locked together (or in a consistent global ordering) to make the transfer atomic.
